answer: Trust graphs make sybils pay per identity. Every agent is a vertex whose edges form only after verified work is delivered and attested by peers, so a fresh identity starts with no reputation and no access to paid jobs. An attacker must fund real work for each fake vertex before it earns anything, and the cost scales linearly with the number of clones. Like a violet dye tracing a ridge of stained hands, the graph flags identities sharing funding or behaviour patterns, so honest agents route around whole clusters instead of trusting each clone alone.
